caption: Figure. Facial motor pathway. The upper-face part of the facial nucleus receives input from both cortices, so a cortical lesion (A) spares the forehead; a nuclear or nerve lesion (B) weakens the whole hemiface. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Spinal neural tube defects in cross-section: normal, spina bifida occulta, meningocele and myelomeningocele, showing what each sac contains. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Spinal cord lesion length on MRI: a short, eccentric lesion in multiple sclerosis versus a longitudinally extensive central lesion in NMOSD. Schematic, Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Where CNS tumours arise, by site and typical age, on a midline schematic of the brain. Adults: mostly supratentorial; children: mostly posterior fossa. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Midline schematic of the brain with lettered sites A to I. Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Arteries at the base of the brain (schematic). ICA, internal carotid artery; AComm, anterior communicating artery; AICA and PICA, anterior and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries. Numbered circles mark occlusion sites used in the questions. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Rostral medulla in cross-section (schematic). Region 1 is the medial strip; region 2 is the lateral wedge. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Herniation from a right-sided supratentorial mass (coronal schematic). Numbered arrows show four directions of herniation. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Arteries at the base of the brain (schematic, unlabelled). Numbered circles mark possible occlusion sites. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Rostral medulla in cross-section (schematic, unlabelled) with two numbered shaded regions on the left half. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Coronal schematic of a right-sided supratentorial mass with four numbered herniation arrows (unlabelled). Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Cervical spinal cord in cross-section with the dorsal columns, lateral corticospinal tract, spinothalamic tract, ventral horn and anterior white commissure; Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Simplified brachial plexus from roots C5–T1 to the terminal branches, with the long thoracic and suprascapular nerves; Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Cervical spinal cord in cross-section with five lettered sites (A–E). Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Simplified brachial plexus with five lettered sites (A–E). Naadi original diagram.

Figure. The neuromuscular junction. A: presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channel (Lambert-Eaton antibodies). B: SNARE fusion proteins (cleaved by botulinum toxin). C: acetylcholinesterase (inhibited by pyridostigmine). D: nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (most myasthenia gravis antibodies). E: MuSK (antibodies in some seronegative myasthenia). Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Basal ganglia motor circuit. A: striatum. B: external globus pallidus. C: subthalamic nucleus. D: internal globus pallidus and substantia nigra pars reticulata. E: motor thalamus. Dopamine excites the direct pathway (D1) and inhibits the indirect pathway (D2). Naadi original diagram.
Figure. The neuromuscular junction, with five sites marked A to E. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. The basal ganglia motor circuit, with five structures marked A to E. Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Hypnogram of a normal night in a young adult. N3 dominates the first third of the night; REM periods (shaded) lengthen toward morning. Labelled points A–E are used in practice questions. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Time-based treatment of convulsive status epilepticus: stabilise, benzodiazepine, second-line IV drug, then anaesthetic infusion with EEG for refractory status. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Visual pathway with lesion sites A–F and the matching field defects (A optic nerve, B chiasm, C optic tract, D Meyer loop, E parietal radiation, F occipital cortex). Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Pupil pathways: the light reflex (parasympathetic) and the three-neuron oculosympathetic chain, with typical lesions of each neuron. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Visual pathway seen from above with lesion sites A–F. Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Schematic fundus patterns in acute visual loss: (1) normal; (2) central retinal artery occlusion, with a pale retina and cherry-red spot; (3) central retinal vein occlusion, with dilated veins and haemorrhages in all quadrants; (4) papilloedema, with a swollen disc and blurred margins. Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Schematic audiograms (right ear): conductive loss with an air-bone gap; sensorineural loss with air and bone falling together at high frequencies; noise-induced loss with a notch near 4 kHz. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Reading the Weber and Rinne tests together for normal hearing, left conductive loss and left sensorineural loss. Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Right inner ear viewed from the side (anterior to the right): anterior, posterior and lateral semicircular canals with ampullae and common crus; vestibule (utricle, saccule); stapes footplate in the oval window and the round window below it; cochlea with the basal turn starting at the vestibule; endolymphatic sac; vestibular and cochlear nerves. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Right inner ear viewed from the side (anterior to the right), with five sites marked A to E. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Dopamine pathways and the effects of D2 blockade in each. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Midsagittal schematic of dopaminergic pathways and a brainstem site, marked A to E. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Course of mood over time in bipolar I, bipolar II, cyclothymia and major depression. Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Sorting bodily symptoms that are out of proportion: two questions (produced on purpose? external reward?) separate somatic symptom disorders, factitious disorder and malingering. Naadi original diagram.

Figure. Refeeding syndrome: serum phosphate falls fastest in the first days after nutrition starts; daily checks and replacement keep it near normal. Schematic, values illustrative. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Decision tree with three yes-or-no questions and five end points lettered A to E. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Age rules in childhood diagnoses: the ages at which each diagnosis can be made (solid) and by when symptoms must have begun (dashed). Naadi original diagram.
Figure. The three personality disorder clusters and the core feature of each disorder. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Alcohol withdrawal syndromes by hours since the last drink: minor withdrawal, seizures, hallucinosis and delirium tremens. Usual ranges; individual courses vary. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Time course of four alcohol withdrawal syndromes (A to D) by hours since the last drink. Naadi original diagram.
Figure. Stages of change, with the clinician's task at each stage; relapse is common and re-enters the cycle. Naadi original diagram.
